title: Inquest rules on shooting death
article: A coroner's jury made several recommendations to help prevent the deaths of mentally ill people like Byron Debassige, who was shot dead by police after he stole lemons from a store.
Debassige, who had substance abuse problems and was diagnosed as a schizophrenic, pulled a knife on the staff at the store near Yonge St. and Davisville Ave. after stealing the lemons.
Shortly after, in a nearby park, he came at police with the knife and was shot four times.
His blood-alcohol level was three times over the legal limit to drive at the time.
The coroner's jury recommends the Ministry of Health create a single organization to deal with mental health and addiction services.

"The Ministry of Health and Long-Term Care should make funding available for the creation of additional teams which provide comprehensive comunitybased psychiatric treatment and support, commonly referred to as Assertive Community Treatment teams to serve mentally disordered people in the community," the jury wrote.

"The Ministry of Health and Long- Term Care should revisit the Mental Health Act to consider whether the legislation criteria for a Community Treatment Order are too restrictive, with the specific recommendation that it should be adjusted to encompass those who have been inmates in correctional psychiatric facilities," it added.

The jury also said the Ministry of Community Safety and Correctional Services needs a diversion program composed of judges, police, lawyers and mental health specialists to oversee people with mental illness in trouble with the law so they can decide if there should be an alternative to traditional sentencing.
The case loads of probation officers should also be reviewed, especially for high-risk clients living in the community.
"Correctional Services should revisit the benefits of having the portion of the curriculum dealing with mental health issues taught by a mental health professional."
Coroner's inquests do not find guilt or innocence.
